subject: Economy
sub_topic: IBBI — Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India

concepts.name: IBC 2016: Legislative Genesis and Policy Rationale
key_dimensions: Pre-IBC fragmented framework: SICA, SARFAESI, RDDBFI — overlaps and failures
Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee (BLRC) under T.K. Viswanathan — key recommendations
Consolidation of 12+ laws into a single code — what was repealed vs. amended
Constitutional backing: Entry 9 (Insolvency) in Concurrent List vs. Centre's overriding jurisdiction

concepts.name: IBBI: Establishment, Composition, and Regulatory Character
key_dimensions: Established under Section 188 of IBC 2016 — statutory body, not a constitutional one
Composition: Chairperson + 5 whole-time members + 3 ex-officio members (RBI, SEBI, MCA nominees) — quorum trap
Dual role as regulator AND oversight body — unique among Indian regulators
Headquarters in New Delhi; accountability to Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA)

concepts.name: IBBI's Regulatory Jurisdiction: Entities and Professionals
key_dimensions: Three regulated entities: Insolvency Professionals (IPs), Insolvency Professional Agencies (IPAs), Information Utilities (IUs)
Insolvency Professional Entities (IPEs) added later — distinction from IPs and IPAs
IBBI does NOT directly regulate Adjudicating Authorities (NCLT/DRT) — common confusion
Jurisdiction over processes: CIRP, Liquidation, Pre-packaged Insolvency, Personal Insolvency

concepts.name: Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP): Trigger Mechanisms
key_dimensions: Default threshold: ₹1 crore (raised from ₹1 lakh during COVID — Section 4 amendment)
Who can initiate: Financial Creditor (Section 7), Operational Creditor (Section 9), Corporate Debtor itself (Section 10)
Key distinction: Financial Creditor files jointly; Operational Creditor must give 10-day demand notice first
UPSC trap: Homebuyers classified as Financial Creditors via 2018 amendment — Chitra Sharma case

concepts.name: Timeline and Moratorium under CIRP
key_dimensions: Original 180-day timeline + 90-day extension = 270 days; amended to mandatory 330-day outer limit including litigation
Section 14 Moratorium: What is prohibited (suits, asset transfer, foreclosure) vs. what continues (supply of essential goods)
NCLT admits application within 14 days — deemed admission if not decided in time (amendment trap)
Swiss Ribbons case (SC 2019): Upheld constitutional validity of IBC and differentiation between financial and operational creditors

concepts.name: Committee of Creditors (CoC): Composition, Voting, and Powers
key_dimensions: CoC comprises only Financial Creditors — Operational Creditors have NO voting rights (only representation rights above threshold)
Voting threshold: Routine decisions 51%; key decisions (resolution plan approval, liquidation) 66%
Related party Financial Creditors: Excluded from CoC — Section 21(2) trap
CoC's commercial wisdom doctrine: Supreme Court in Essar Steel case — courts cannot interfere with CoC decisions on merit

concepts.name: Insolvency Resolution Professional (IRP) and Resolution Professional (RP): Roles and Accountability
key_dimensions: IRP appointed by NCLT on admission; CoC can replace IRP with RP by 66% vote
RP takes over management of Corporate Debtor — Board of Directors suspended (Section 17)
RP's functions: Public announcement, collation of claims, managing operations as going concern, inviting resolution plans
IBBI disciplinary mechanism over IPs: Inspection, investigation, and adjudication — three-stage process

concepts.name: Resolution Plan: Eligibility, Content, and Approval
key_dimensions: Section 29A: Ineligibility criteria for resolution applicants — promoters with NPA accounts, wilful defaulters, convicted persons
Section 29A controversy: Arcelormittal vs. Satish Kumar Gupta (SC) — strict interpretation of connected persons
Resolution plan must provide for operational creditors at least liquidation value — waterfall mechanism compliance
Approved plan binding on all stakeholders including dissenting creditors and government dues (Ghanashyam Mishra case)

concepts.name: Liquidation Process under IBC: Initiation and Waterfall Mechanism
key_dimensions: Liquidation triggered when: No resolution plan in time, CoC decides (66%), resolution plan contravenes law

Section 53 Waterfall: CIRP costs → secured creditors (with security) → workmen dues (24 months) → other employee dues → unsecured financial creditors → government dues → remaining secured creditors → equity
Government dues rank BELOW unsecured financial creditors — reversal of traditional priority (UPSC trap)
Liquidation vs. going concern sale — liquidator can sell as going concern to maximize value

concepts.name: Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP): For MSMEs
key_dimensions: Introduced via IBC Amendment 2021 — applicable only to MSMEs (default between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore)
Key distinction from CIRP: Debtor-in-possession model vs. creditor-in-control in CIRP
Base Resolution Plan submitted by promoter before approaching NCLT — creditors approve before admission
Timeline: 120 days (faster than CIRP's 330 days) — preserves business relationships and reduces stigma

concepts.name: Personal Insolvency and Bankruptcy: Fresh Start, IRP, and Bankruptcy
key_dimensions: Part III of IBC: Three processes for individuals/partnership firms — Fresh Start Process, Insolvency Resolution Process, Bankruptcy
Fresh Start: For individuals with annual income ≤ ₹60,000 and assets ≤ ₹20,000 and qualifying debt ≤ ₹35,000
Adjudicating Authority for individuals: Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT), NOT NCLT — critical distinction
Parts III and IV of IBC not yet fully notified/operational — examiner's trap on what is 'live'

concepts.name: Information Utilities (IUs): Role and Significance
key_dimensions: IUs store financial information of debtors — lenders submit data; accessible to all stakeholders
NeSL (National e-Governance Services Ltd.) — only operational IU currently
Purpose: Reduce information asymmetry, speed up claims verification, prevent fraudulent claims
IBBI regulates IUs under IBC Section 210 — registration, data standards, access norms

concepts.name: Insolvency Professional Agencies (IPAs): Governance of IPs
key_dimensions: IPAs are self-regulatory organizations (SROs) under IBBI — enroll and regulate IPs
Three recognized IPAs: ICSI-IIP (ICSI), IIIPI (IBA promoted), ICAI-IIP (ICAI) — membership-based
IBBI regulates IPAs; IPAs regulate IPs — two-tier regulatory architecture
Difference from IPs: IPA is institutional body; IP is individual professional — common confusion in questions

concepts.name: Adjudicating Authorities: NCLT and DRT — Jurisdiction and Appeals
key_dimensions: NCLT: Adjudicates for companies and LLPs; DRT: For individuals and partnership firms
Appeals from NCLT → NCLAT → Supreme Court (on question of law only)
Appeals from DRT → DRAT → High Court → Supreme Court
IBBI is NOT an appellate authority — it is purely regulatory; courts handle disputes

concepts.name: Cross-Border Insolvency: UNCITRAL Model Law and India's Position
key_dimensions: IBC Sections 234 and 235: Enable bilateral agreements for cross-border insolvency — not yet fully operationalized
UNCITRAL Model Law on Cross-Border Insolvency 1997 — India has NOT yet adopted it (as of knowledge cutoff)
Insolvency Law Committee 2018 recommended adoption of UNCITRAL Model Law with modifications
Key principles of Model Law: Centre of Main Interests (COMI), modified universalism, cooperation between jurisdictions

concepts.name: IBBI's Powers: Inspection, Investigation, and Enforcement
key_dimensions: IBBI can inspect IPs, IPAs, IUs suo motu or on complaint — Section 218
Investigation powers: Appoint investigating authority, examine records, call for information
Penalties: Warning, suspension/cancellation of registration, monetary penalty up to ₹1 crore or 3x illegal gains
Quasi-judicial function: Adjudicating Officer mechanism within IBBI for disciplinary proceedings — separation of functions

concepts.name: Key Supreme Court Judgments Shaping IBC Jurisprudence
key_dimensions: Swiss Ribbons (2019): Constitutional validity upheld; differentiation between financial and operational creditors justified
Essar Steel (2019): CoC's commercial wisdom is supreme; equal treatment does not mean identical treatment for all creditors
Vidarbha Industries (2022): NCLT has discretion to admit or reject Section 7 application — not automatic on proof of default (controversial)
Committee of Creditors of Essar Steel vs. Satish Kumar Gupta: Resolution plan binding on all including Central/State government dues

concepts.name: IBC vs. SARFAESI vs. DRT: Overlap, Priority, and Coordination
key_dimensions: IBC overrides SARFAESI during moratorium period — Section 14 stays SARFAESI enforcement
Secured creditor's choice: Relinquish security to liquidation estate OR realize security outside liquidation (Section 52)
IBC does NOT repeal SARFAESI — both coexist; SARFAESI faster for single secured creditor outside insolvency
UPSC trap: SARFAESI applies to secured creditors with ≥₹1 lakh debt; IBC threshold is ₹1 crore for companies

concepts.name: Resolution of Financial Service Providers (FSPs) under IBC
key_dimensions: FSPs (banks, NBFCs, insurance) NOT covered under regular IBC — Section 227 empowers government to notify special rules
FRDI Bill 2017 (withdrawn) vs. IBC FSP Rules 2019 — different approaches to financial firm resolution
FSP insolvency: Administrator appointed (not RP); respective regulator (RBI/IRDAI/SEBI) involved in nomination
IL&FS, DHFL, Yes Bank resolutions tested FSP provisions — each used different mechanism highlighting regulatory gaps

concepts.name: Voluntary Liquidation and Fast-Track CIRP: Alternate Processes
key_dimensions: Voluntary Liquidation (Section 59): Solvent company winding up — requires shareholder resolution + declaration of solvency; NOT insolvency
Fast Track CIRP (Section 55): For small companies, startups (<2 years), unlisted companies with assets ≤₹1 crore — 90-day timeline
Key trap: Voluntary liquidation ≠ insolvency; company must be solvent and able to pay debts
Fast Track CIRP rarely used in practice — IBBI data shows low uptake; examiner may test awareness of underutilized provisions
